content.comment_body: How can I connect an electronic circuit to a [product_name] controller? I have built a rain drop sensor using electronic components. Is it possible to use this sensor as an input in my program, and if so, how?
There is no [product_name] model labeled 230RC X50; the X50 refers to the mSD card slot. You haven't specified the output signal from your electronic device. Please provide more precise details.
Apologies, I made a mistake. My actual model number is [article_no]. Here is my sensor: [IMAGE]
No, you can't directly connect the sensor to your [product_name] controller because the sensor uses a 12VDC power supply. You need to include an opto coupler or a relay in your sensor circuit.
Can you suggest which relay I should use?
Could you provide a wiring diagram showing how to connect my sensor output to the input of the [product_name] controller?

Should I just remove the battery? Also, if possible, could you specify the exact model of component I need to buy to make this connection to the [product_name] controller? I would appreciate your help.
Why do you want to remove the battery? It's needed for powering both your sensor electronics and the relay. If you remove the battery, you'll need to provide an alternate 12VDC power supply.
Yes, I am using an AC to DC converter power supply. So, does that drawing apply to an optocoupler for the [product_name] controller, or something else?
That drawing is for a relay setup.

If you aren't sure how to implement the provided relay diagram, it might be safer to use a [product_name] controller suited for low voltage instead of an AC230V variant. If you're not a qualified electrician, attempting this could pose safety risks.
Who are you referring to? The user with the nickname '[user_name]' or me? Please clarify by mentioning the relevant username.

If you meant my comment, it was intended as a precaution regarding mixing DC12/24V and AC230V voltages. It's generally better to use low voltage throughout if possible, which would only require a mains adapter for the controller and all components operating at low voltage. Another option is to use a rain sensor with an AC230V supply and a potential-free output suitable for AC230V. This way, all components would use AC230V and the rain sensor would remain internally isolated.
